one_line: The first paper in this corpus to put the sleep-round index $k$ on the x-axis of a real LLM loop and print a no-memory reference line beside it — and the answer it gets is that repeated (U-E) is a net loss, that it is a net loss even when every input trajectory is a ground-truth solution, and that an episodic-only control which never runs $S(\cdot;B_s)$ at all beats the consolidators in 26 of 28 measured cells.

problem_stated.as_the_paper_frames_it: Agentic-memory systems 'pursue the consolidated form: an LLM rewrites past trajectories into a textual memory bank that it continuously updates with new interactions, promising self-improving agents without parameter updates. Yet we find that such consolidated memories produced by today's LLMs are often faulty even when derived from useful experiences.' [Abstract, p.1]
problem_stated.the_assumption_it_attacks: 'Many recent agentic-memory systems—CLIN (Majumder et al., 2023), Agent Workflow Memory (Wang et al., 2024), Dynamic Cheatsheet (Suzgun et al., 2026), and ACE (Zhang et al., 2025)—adopt update-after-every-interaction designs that treat each consolidation step as at worst neutral; our results contradict this assumption.' [§1, p.3]
problem_stated.the_experimental_move: Make the inputs demonstrably useful by construction, so that any regression must be attributable to the write operator rather than to the data: 'we study settings in which the input trajectories are demonstrably useful: either drawn from problems the agent has already solved without memory, or supplied with ground-truth solutions.' [§1, p.2]
problem_stated.the_attribution_argument: 'Because the trajectory pool is held fixed across these comparisons, the variance across schedules and the episodic-only control together point to the consolidation step itself, not the underlying experience, as the source of the failure.' [§1, p.2]
problem_stated.note_writer_remark: [note-writer] This is the corpus's first paper whose object of study is the write operator $\mathrm{wr}$ of (U-E) rather than a system built on it. Every other $E$-path note in `notes/stc-v2/` records a system proposing a write rule; this one holds the data fixed and varies the rule.

core_mechanism.one_line_unified: The paper does not propose a new (U-E); it instruments the existing one. It holds the experience pool $\mathcal{H}$ fixed and varies (i) the number of rounds $k$, (ii) the batch $m$ of trajectories fed per round, (iii) whether the store is split into $E^{\mathrm{epi}} \oplus E^{\mathrm{abs}}$, and (iv) whether $S(\cdot;B_s)$ is mandatory, optional, or disabled — then measures held-out quality as a function of $k$ against a no-memory reference line.

outer_vs_inner.reader_takeaway: [note-writer] For the monograph reader the useful contrast is with `letta-stc`: there, the sole moving part was one text block moved once. Here the sole moving part is a text bank moved 200 times, and the paper's finding is that the 200th state is worse than the 1st and, in two of three rollouts, no better than never having moved anything. Same layer, same absence of gradients, opposite conclusion — and the difference between the two papers is exactly the round index $k$.

update_layer.instantiates: (U-E) — and only (U-E). Explicitly and by declared scope.
how_this_paper_differs_from_the_canonica: $k$ IS THE INDEPENDENT VARIABLE. Every other $E$-path note in this corpus records $k$ as fixed (Letta STC: $k=1$ always; Mem0/Zep/ReasoningBank: $k$ grows but is never an axis). Here $k$ runs to 200 consolidation stages [App. G.1], 190 update steps [App. D.5], 250 steps [App. D.5 Example 2], 400 stream steps [Fig. 5], and 100 distill iterations [Fig. 8a], with quality printed at intervals against a no-memory line.

$\mathrm{wr}$ IS A TYPED ACTION SET, not a fixed operator: $\{$Retain, Delete, Consolidate$\}$, chosen per round by the frozen model [§3, p.5]. Retain is the operation the rest of the corpus's write alphabets omit — Mem0 has ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NOOP, Letta STC has destructive overwrite only, ReasoningBank has pure union. None of them can express 'keep this raw'.

$E$ IS SPLIT into $E^{\mathrm{epi}} \oplus E^{\mathrm{abs}}$ with independent caps, so $S(\cdot;B_s)$ can be ablated OUT while (U-E) keeps running [FM7]. This makes the offline-inference term separable from the offline-selection term for the first time in the corpus.

$S(\cdot;B_s)$ IS THE TREATMENT, NOT THE METHOD. The paper's control conditions differ 'only in how trajectories are presented to the memory manager' [§3, p.4] — same data, same model, same eval. That is the design the book's ch25 §25.2.1 says nobody ran.

THE STORE IS CAPPED AND THE CAP BINDS. ALFWorld: 50 items, and the paper attributes a specific lost meta-strategy to eviction ('The 50-item cap evicted it to make room for paraphrases of the desklamp template' [App. G.1, p.52]). ScienceWorld: explicit FIFO with the cap announced to the LLM in the prompt [App. F.3, p.47]. This is the corpus's first $E$-path paper where capacity pressure is instrumented rather than ignored.

$\mathrm{ret}$ IS STILL THE IDENTITY. 'we provide all memory entries in context' [§3, p.4]. So the paper measures the store's content quality without any retrieval confound — which is exactly why the negative result cannot be blamed on a retriever.

B_s.value: absent in the required units (FLOPs or tokens); proxies printed
B_s.detail: No token count, FLOP count, dollar figure, or call-cost anywhere. The paper's only acknowledgement of cost is a constraint on itself: 'due to API-cost constraints we report point estimates from a small number of repeats per question rather than formal error bars' [§8, p.11]. PROXIES THAT ARE PRINTED, and they are better than most of the corpus: (a) 'The abstraction makes 3 LLM calls per trajectory' [App. F.1, p.45] — so the ALFWorld n=128 golden set costs 768 × 3 = 2304 abstraction calls before any consolidation round begins [본서 산술]; (b) 200 consolidation stages × 1 full-memory rewrite each, each conditioned on 6 abstracts [App. G.1, p.50]; (c) 190 update steps for the ARC-AGI 19-task × 10-pass run [App. D.5, p.41]; (d) 20 rounds over 485 rollouts in mini-batches for ScienceWorld [App. F.3, p.47; App. J.1.3, p.65]; (e) 3 epochs at batch size 16 over 128 trajectories for WebShop AWM [App. H.1.2, p.58]; (f) 400 steps for the ARC-AGI Stream [Fig. 5, p.7].
B_s.finding: This is the corpus's most COUNTABLE $B_s$ and still not a reportable one. Call counts × round counts are multiplicable to a call budget but not to tokens, and the paper's whole normative claim ('gate consolidation explicitly rather than firing it after every interaction' [Abstract]) is a claim about how to SPEND $B_s$ made without ever measuring $B_s$. The chapter must say this plainly: a paper telling the field to stop wasting offline compute prints no offline-compute figure.

L_w.detail: Zero wall-clock, TTFT, ms/token, or latency figures. The only time-like quantities are step counts inside episodes: `max_steps=50` (ALFWorld) [App. F.1, p.45], `eval_max_steps=30` (WebShop) [App. I.1, p.59], and mean trajectory length in steps (12.4 / 11.4 for gpt-5.4-mini; 18.2 / 15.8 for gpt-5-mini) [Table 12, p.61].
L_w.the_one_wake_side_number_that_matters: Table 12's mean-steps column is the closest thing to a wake-cost measurement in the paper, and it moves the RIGHT way when memory is REMOVED: deleting one workflow (W8) from the consolidated memory cuts mean steps from 12.4 to 11.4 and from 18.2 to 15.8, and cuts step-cap hits from 22/50 to 17/50 [Table 12, p.61]. [본서 관찰] A faulty $E$ entry costs wake-time steps as well as accuracy — the two costs move together, and the paper never says so.

C.detail: Printed values: (a) ALFWorld stage 168 — '50 items totalling 48,506 characters (i.e., the cap is saturated, average ~970 characters per item)' [App. G.2, p.53]; (b) stage 169 — '1 item of 1,960 characters'; (c) stage 170 — '2 items, 3,410 chars'; (d) ACE on WebShop stage 100 — '32 bullets totalling about 14k characters' [App. H.1.1, p.56]; (e) Dynamic Cheatsheet on WebShop stage 100 — 'roughly 8.3k characters' [App. H.1.1, p.57]; (f) AWM on WebShop epoch 3 — '16 workflows, ~8.2k chars' [App. H.1.2, p.58]; (g) stage 20 peak — 42 items, stage 200 — 38 items [App. G.1, pp.50–52]. C.finding: [본서 산술] At the cap, one saturated $E$ store is 48,506 characters ≈ 48.5 KB assuming one byte per character. The book's ch26 anchor for the $E$-path is 56.0 KB per user. The two agree to within 13.4%. That is an INDEPENDENT confirmation of ch26 판정 2's cold-tier placement for $E$ — see book_impact. CAVEATS the chapter must carry: the unit is per-store-per-run, not per-user; no encoding is stated; and the store here is capped by an author-chosen policy rather than by a system's natural growth.

derived_rho_for_the_book.ALFWorld_mean_rate: Qwen3.5-4B: (35−15)/48 = 41.67 pp over 180 stages = 0.231 pp per consolidation stage. Qwen3.5-9B: (35−16)/48 = 39.58 pp over 180 stages = 0.220 pp/stage. Qwen3.5-27B: (41−22)/48 = 39.58 pp over 200 stages = 0.198 pp/stage.
derived_rho_for_the_book.ALFWorld_unit_definition: 1 stage = one full-memory rewrite by gpt-5-nano conditioned on 6 fresh trajectory abstracts (1 per task type), under a 50-item cap, with the whole memory placed in the solver's context at eval.
derived_rho_for_the_book.ARC_AGI_GT_rate: First pass: (100−73.7)/19 updates = 1.384 pp per update. Ten passes: (100−52.6)/190 updates = 0.249 pp per update. Passes 2–10 alone: (73.7−52.6)/171 = 0.123 pp per update, i.e. 2.34 pp per pass. The rate is strongly SUBLINEAR in $k$ — most of the damage is done in the first pass.
derived_rho_for_the_book.instantaneous_maximum: A single consolidation stage (S=168 → 169, 50 items → 1 item) costs 6/48 = 12.5 pp (4B), 10/48 = 20.83 pp (9B), 13/48 = 27.08 pp (27B) [Table 11, p.53]. Against the ALFWorld mean rates above, that is 54× to 137× the mean. $\rho$ IS NOT A CONSTANT IN $k$ — this single comparison is the strongest empirical support in the corpus for ch29 판정 5.
derived_rho_for_the_book.K_star: Qwen3.5-4B and 9B: $k^\ast = 20$ stages. Qwen3.5-27B: $k^\ast = 0$ — 'the 27B rollout's peak is the un-consolidated base seed at stage 0 (41/48), so consolidation never helps it' [Fig. 16 caption, p.51].
derived_rho_for_the_book.the_control_that_matters_most: Static R10 = Static R50 = 94.7% [Fig. 2, p.5]. Forty additional whole-pool refreshes cost ZERO. So at matched data and matched refresh count, $\rho_{\text{Static}} \approx 0.0$ pp per refresh (after an initial 5.3 pp = 1/19 problems) while $\rho_{\text{Stream}} = 0.249$ pp per update. The schedule-only gap at $k_{\mathrm{pass}}=10$ is 94.7 − 52.6 = 42.1 pp. [본서 산술] **$\rho$ is not a property of repetition. It is a property of incrementality — of rewriting a rewrite instead of re-deriving from the preserved pool.**

rho.why_it_is_still_not_a_filled_cell_under_: ch25 §25.2 requires 'a number with the required unit printed in the source'; for $\rho$ the required unit is a per-round loss rate. This paper prints $\mathrm{Acc}(E_k)$, not $\rho$. Under the strict rule the cell holds a 대용치 (round-axis curve + no-memory reference line), not a fill. Under ch25 §25.5's stated falsifier — 'sleep 라운드 수를 독립변수로 놓은 실험에서 인쇄하는 경우' — the condition IS met. The chapter must make that call in one sentence rather than leave it ambiguous.

N_q.detail: There is no $N_q$ in this design: the store is not built for a single context shared by several queries but for a task family shared by a held-out split. The closest analogue is the eval-set size (48 ALFWorld episodes / 50 WebShop sessions / 100 AppWorld tasks / 44 ScienceWorld cases / 50 held-out ARC-AGI tasks), across which the one consolidated store is amortised. All GPT-5.4-family and Claude models are closed APIs with undisclosed parameter counts. So the paper's only parameter-indexed axis is the three Qwen sizes, and on that axis the erosion result is size-robust in direction and size-INVERTED in magnitude: the largest rollout loses the most from a bad consolidation step (−13 wins vs −6) and is the only one for which consolidation never helps at all [Fig. 16 caption, p.51; Table 11, p.53].

scale_ceiling.round_scale: THE PAPER'S REAL CEILING, AND IT IS THE HIGHEST IN THE CORPUS. 200 consolidation stages (ALFWorld), 400 stream steps (ARC-AGI), 250 single-pass steps and 190 update steps (ARC-AGI GT), 192 stages (ACE on WebShop), 100 distill iterations (Fig. 8a), 20 full passes over 485 rollouts (ScienceWorld), 3 epochs × 128 trajectories (WebShop AWM). Compare: every other $E$-path paper in `notes/stc-v2/` runs $k=1$ (Letta STC) or leaves $k$ unreported.
scale_ceiling.evaluation_scale: Smallest and most load-bearing: the 19-problem ARC-AGI slice behind the headline (one problem = 5.26 pp). Then 33 → no; 44 ScienceWorld cases; 48 ALFWorld episodes; 50 WebShop sessions; 50 held-out ARC-AGI tasks; 100 AppWorld tasks. Largest training pool: 768 ALFWorld trajectories (n=128 golden × 6 types).
scale_ceiling.context_length_ceiling: Not reported as a length. The nearest quantity is the store size in characters (48,506 max) plus the full trajectory-log baselines placed in context ('All' = the entire pool of summarized rollouts). AppWorld entries are explicitly summarized 'to keep per-entry length tractable for prompt-time concatenation' [App. F.4, p.49] — an admission that the raw-log baseline would not fit, with no length figure attached.
scale_ceiling.realism_ceiling: Four public agent benchmarks plus one synthetic testbed the authors built. The authors state the boundary themselves: 'whether the same erosion dynamics appear in embodied, multi-modal, or tool-rich production settings remains open' [§8, p.11]. No deployed system, no real user traffic, no production memory store is examined.
scale_ceiling.deployment_gap: [note-writer] The paper's normative claim is about production defaults ('robust agent memory should treat raw episodes as first-class evidence and gate consolidation explicitly rather than firing it after every interaction' [Abstract]) and its evidence is 48–100 held-out items per cell at single-run point estimates. The claim is one order of magnitude broader than the evidence — which is the same complaint this book files against the $E$-path systems, applied to their critic.

inherited_open_question.verdict: STATED, and unusually cleanly — this paper inherits a testable PREDICTION and tests it. That makes it one of very few papers in this corpus with a textbook bridge-in.
inherited_open_question.the_inherited_assumption_it_falsifies: 'Many recent agentic-memory systems—CLIN (Majumder et al., 2023), Agent Workflow Memory (Wang et al., 2024), Dynamic Cheatsheet (Suzgun et al., 2026), and ACE (Zhang et al., 2025)—adopt update-after-every-interaction designs that treat each consolidation step as at worst neutral; our results contradict this assumption.' [§1, p.3]
inherited_open_question.the_inherited_prediction_it_tests: 'Following the Complementary Learning Systems framing (McClelland et al., 1995; Sun et al., 2023; Tse et al., 2007), we maintain two stores: an Episodic buffer of problem–solution pairs and an Abstract store of consolidated lessons; the control conditions below are designed to test this gating prediction directly.' [§3, p.5]. The prediction is spelled out in §5: 'Complementary Learning Systems make this prescription explicitly: a fast episodic store and a slow schema-forming store are kept architecturally distinct so that fast learning does not overwrite the slow one, and consolidation is gated by schema fit rather than triggered on every event (McClelland et al., 1995; Kumaran et al., 2016; Tse et al., 2007; Sun et al., 2023). The Force regime collapses this separation into a mandatory rewrite loop, recreating the interference conditions the dual-system design was meant to prevent (McCloskey and Cohen, 1989; French, 1999).' [§5, p.8]
inherited_open_question.the_second_inherited_claim: 'Schema formation is beneficial when new evidence fits existing structure (Tse et al., 2007), but harmful when it is non-selective or poorly controlled: nonselective consolidation causes interference and loss of specificity (McClelland et al., 1995; Sun et al., 2023).' [§2, p.4]. The paper's whole design is the LLM instantiation of that conditional.
inherited_open_question.what_it_does_NOT_inherit: It does not cite Letta's `Sleep-time Compute` (2504.13171) and never uses the phrase. Its only Letta citation is the software documentation ('Letta: Stateful agents framework, 2024. URL https://www.letta.com'), listed among forms of 'hierarchical context stores' beside MemGPT [§2, p.3; References, p.12]. So the $E$-path's founding-name paper is invisible to the paper that measures the $E$-path's write operator over 200 rounds.
inherited_open_question.bridge_in_material_for_the_chapter: [note-writer] This is the corpus's counterexample to ch23 §23.8. Here the biology arrives as an ARGUMENT — a named prediction, an architecture derived from it, and control conditions built to test it — and the WORD does not arrive at all ('sleep' appears zero times in the paper). The book's finding was '이름은 생물학에서 왔고 논증은 오지 않았다'; this paper is the exact mirror. The chapter should place the two side by side rather than treat this as a refutation.

open_questions.bridge_out: No gate signal is specified anywhere. 'Auto' is not a gate — it is the same LLM choosing freely, and its choices are shown to be cap-dependent [Fig. 7c]. Compare Letta STC's $\log P(q\mid c)$ predictability signal, which is at least a proposal.

open_questions.question: Do the erosion dynamics survive outside text-only agent benchmarks?
open_questions.exact_wording: 'whether the same erosion dynamics appear in embodied, multi-modal, or tool-rich production settings remains open'

open_questions.question: Does parametric memory suffer the same failure?
open_questions.exact_wording: 'parametric memory (weight updates, distillation into the model) and structured non-textual memory representations are out of scope'
open_questions.bridge_out: An explicit hand-off of the $\Theta$-path question, made without running a single $\Theta$-path baseline. This is the cross-path silence in its most polite form.

open_questions.question: Would a consolidator fine-tuned for the job avoid the failure?
open_questions.exact_wording: 'the consolidator and the solver are themselves LLMs, so faulty abstraction reflects current model capability and could shift with stronger consolidators or with consolidator-specific fine-tuning'
open_questions.bridge_out: the paper's own escape hatch, and the one place it gestures at (U-$\Theta$) — training the write operator rather than prompting it.

open_questions.question: What architecture keeps the episodic and schema-forming roles distinct?
open_questions.exact_wording: 'our results motivate architectures that keep the episodic and abstraction-forming roles distinct rather than collapsing both into a single rewrite loop'
open_questions.bridge_out: named, not built. The two-store split of ARC-AGI Stream is a testbed, not a proposed system.

open_questions.question: Why does grouping by task family help, and can it be automated?
open_questions.status: The paper shows Static-Group > Static-All and that segmentation capability exists but is slow (71 steps / 568 examples to admit all six families), yet proposes no segmentation procedure.

open_questions.question: What is the cost of any of this?
open_questions.status: not addressed. Zero tokens, FLOPs, dollars, or wall-clock in a paper whose recommendation is a compute-allocation policy.

unfavorable_facts.fact: THE HEADLINE NUMBER IS PRINTED THREE INCOMPATIBLE WAYS, and the Abstract's version is the complement of the body's.
unfavorable_facts.the_four_renderings: Abstract: 'GPT-5.4 fails on 54% of a set of ARC-AGI problems it had previously solved without memory' [p.1] ⇒ success 46%. §1: 'it then fails on 46% of them (Fig. 2)' [p.2] ⇒ success 54%. §4.1: 'brings GPT-5.4 down to 54% on the very problems it had previously solved (Fig. 2)' [p.5] ⇒ success 54%, fails 46%. Figure 2 itself: 52.6% success ⇒ fails 47.4%.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: The Abstract states the complement of what the body states — one of the two is simply wrong — and neither matches the figure the sentence cites. On 19 problems, 54%, 46% and 52.6% are 10.3, 8.7 and 10.0 problems, so the discrepancy is not rounding. This is the paper's single most quoted number.

unfavorable_facts.fact: The cleanest, most-cited result rests on n = 19 problems, evaluated once, with no error bars.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: One problem = 5.263 pp. The Static-vs-Stream gap at R10 (94.7 vs 52.6) is 8 problems; the Stream R1-to-R10 decline (73.7 → 52.6) is 4 problems. The paper's own Limitations concede 'point estimates from a small number of repeats per question rather than formal error bars'.

unfavorable_facts.fact: The 'double the accuracy' claim appears ONLY in the Abstract and is supported by no numeric statement anywhere in the body.
unfavorable_facts.exact_wording: 'agents preserve raw episodes by default and double the accuracy of their forced-consolidation counterparts' [Abstract, p.1]. A whole-text search finds 'double' nowhere else except ARC-AGI grid descriptions. §5's three observations are entirely qualitative: 'generally outperforms Force', 'matches or exceeds the full Auto mode', 'collapses accuracy back to the no-memory baseline'.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: A 2× factor in the abstract that the reader must reconstruct by eye from Fig. 5 or Fig. 9a. The book forbids exactly this in §6.4.
unfavorable_facts.source: [Abstract p.1; §5 pp.7–8; Figs. 5 p.7 and 9 p.10]

unfavorable_facts.fact: The Force arm changes TWO things at once, so the paper's central causal conclusion is not isolated by its own design.
unfavorable_facts.exact_wording: 'Force requires consolidation each round and no Episodic entries persist between rounds' [§3, p.5]. The conclusion drawn from it: 'both policies that gate abstraction (Auto) and policies that disable it entirely (Episodic Management Only) match or exceed forced abstraction (Force), pointing to mandatory rewriting at every step—rather than abstraction itself—as the decisive failure mode in this regime' [§5, p.8].
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: Force = mandatory abstraction AND mandatory episode deletion. Auto = optional abstraction AND episode retention. The Auto>Force gap therefore cannot distinguish 'forced abstraction hurts' from 'deleting your episodes hurts', and the second is the trivial hypothesis. The missing arm — mandatory consolidation WITH episode retention — is never run. Fig. 9a's 'Auto (Abstract Only)' is not that arm either, since it removes episodes at READ time rather than at WRITE time.

unfavorable_facts.fact: The flagship erosion curve confounds repeated consolidation with a consolidator downgrade, and the control is never run.
unfavorable_facts.exact_wording: 'We first consolidate ALFWorld trajectories with GPT-5.4—the strongest model we test—following the Static-Group setting from §3, then continue updating that store in batches with GPT-5-nano on the same trajectory pool.' [§4.1, p.5]. App. G.1 confirms: the stage-0 seed is a single gpt-5.4 pass; 'Each subsequent stage feeds gpt-5-nano' [p.50].
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: Stage 0 was written by the strongest model and every one of the next 200 stages by a nano model. The decline is therefore consistent with 'nano rewrites are worse than a 5.4 rewrite' without any cumulative effect at all. The paper frames it as 'A strong memory is not a fixed point' — but a fixed-point claim needs the SAME operator applied repeatedly. No gpt-5.4-for-all-200-stages control exists.

unfavorable_facts.fact: No cost accounting of any kind, in a paper whose thesis is a compute-allocation policy.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: Zero tokens, FLOPs, dollars, wall-clock, or latency. The recommendation — 'gate consolidation explicitly rather than firing it after every interaction' — is a claim about when to spend $B_s$, and $B_s$ is never counted. The only cost sentence in the paper is about the authors' own budget: 'due to API-cost constraints'. Under the book's §6.4 rule 3 ('비용 침묵을 성능 주장으로 메우는 것'), this paper commits the mirror error: it fills a cost silence with a quality argument.

unfavorable_facts.fact: The ScienceWorld 'average test score' is negative at rounds 10 and 20 and its scale is never defined.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: ScienceWorld's native score is 0–100. A negative average implies either a delta against an unstated reference or a rescaling, and the paper says only 'we also report the corresponding average test score'. The numbers cannot be placed on any axis in the rest of the paper, and the sign flip between rounds 1 and 10 is the most dramatic degradation figure in the appendix.

unfavorable_facts.fact: A sign/word error in the second-largest reported effect.
unfavorable_facts.exact_wording: 'Cumulative ends +203 points behind Fresh (Fig. 10).' [§6.2, p.10]. The figure labels the same quantity 'Final gap: +203' inside a band labelled 'Fresh advantage', with the Cumulative curve running below zero to about −150.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: '+203 behind' is not a well-formed quantity, the sign convention is never stated, and the score unit is the same undefined ScienceWorld scale as above.

unfavorable_facts.fact: Two of the WebShop consolidator cells score essentially zero and the authors stopped rather than debugged.
unfavorable_facts.exact_wording: 'The results with * are evaluted [sic] by model GPT-5-Mini. Then we observed that its performance were near to 0, so we did not do remaining ACE or DC experiments on webshop.' ACE = 00*, DC = 03* against NoMem = 18.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: A near-zero result from a published method is more likely a harness bug than a finding, and it is left in the table as evidence with an asterisk that also discloses a backbone mismatch (the cells are evaluated by a different model than the row's label). Table 2 and Table 3 are then read as one body of evidence.

unfavorable_facts.fact: The memory cap is a binding, outcome-shaping parameter that is never ablated in the flagship erosion run.
unfavorable_facts.exact_wording: App. G.1 attributes a specific loss to the cap: 'The 50-item cap evicted it to make room for paraphrases of the desklamp template' [p.52]. And 'Memory size stays bounded at 38–50 items by the cap throughout, so the erosion is in content quality, not item count' [p.50].
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: The second sentence argues the cap is not the cause while the first sentence names the cap as the mechanism of the paper's third erosion mode. An uncapped arm exists elsewhere (|M| = ∞ in Fig. 4) but not for the 200-stage curve. Meanwhile App. H.1.2 shows a store that degrades with NO binding cap ('collapse by accretion'), so the paper has both stories and does not reconcile them.

unfavorable_facts.fact: The agent's 'own' episodic-first policy is partly an artefact of the buffer size the authors chose.
unfavorable_facts.exact_wording: Fig. 7c: 'Bigger buffer halves Compress, grows Keep.' Action shares — |Episodic|=50: Keep 58.5%, Compress 32.5%, Remove 9.0%; |Episodic|=100: Keep 60.8%, Compress 18.5%, Remove 20.8%. §5 concludes: 'The Auto-mode result therefore reflects an episodic-first policy that the agent chooses when the architecture permits it.'
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: The write-policy distribution moves with a hyperparameter the authors set, so 'the agent chooses' is conditional on that setting. Also the caption's emphasis is wrong: Keep moves +2.3 pp while Remove moves +11.8 pp.

unfavorable_facts.fact: Mind2Web is named as a studied benchmark twice and produces no result.
unfavorable_facts.exact_wording: 'We study how models abstract memory from experience across clean and widely-used agent benchmarks—ALFWorld, ScienceWorld, WebShop, AppWorld (Trivedi et al., 2024), and Mind2Web (Deng et al., 2023)' [§3, p.4]; repeated in §8's scope conditions [p.11].
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: Table 1's settings list has no Mind2Web row, App. F has no Mind2Web subsection, and no figure or table reports it. The benchmark count in the paper's framing sentence is one larger than the benchmark count in its evidence.

unfavorable_facts.fact: Table 1's figure→setting mapping does not agree with the figure captions.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: Table 1 lists Fig. 2 (an ARC-AGI figure, per its own caption) and Fig. 8a under the AppWorld row, and lists Fig. 8b under AppWorld while its caption reads 'Switch-induced forgetting in ARC-AGI'. A reader reconstructing which benchmark produced which curve cannot rely on the table the paper provides for that purpose.
unfavorable_facts.source: [Table 1, p.3 vs Fig. 2 caption p.5, Fig. 8 caption p.9]

unfavorable_facts.fact: The paper's headline word — that consolidation is the culprit — is not uniformly supported by its own largest table.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: [본서 산술] On ALFWorld, consolidated memory beats no-memory in 9 of 12 consolidator cells and raw trajectory logs take GPT-5.4-Mini from 54% to 92%. On AppWorld the pattern reverses (31 of 40 memory cells below no-memory). The paper pools the two under 'memory utility degrades' and never names benchmark identity as a moderator, although it is the single largest factor in the table.

unfavorable_facts.fact: The LLM judge that supplies the mechanistic account of task-switch interference is unnamed and unvalidated.
unfavorable_facts.exact_wording: 'We use LLM judge to label each memory entry and find Cumulative accumulates overgeneralized memories at ~5× Fresh's rate and garbage memories at ~20×' [§6.2, p.10].
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: The 5× and 20× are the paper's only mechanistic numbers for its interference claim, and the instrument that produces them has no stated model, no prompt in the appendix, no inter-rater check, and no accuracy figure. Compare ReasoningBank's judge, whose 72.7% accuracy the book already flags (→ ch15).

unfavorable_facts.fact: Five different round counters, no conversion table, and one of them is a wake-stream index rather than a round index.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: consolidation stage $S$, refresh round $R$, Distill Iter., epoch, and step all appear as x-axes. The single conversion the reader needs (1 refresh round = 19 updates on the 19-task pool) is buried in App. D.5 and never appears near Fig. 2. Fig. 5's 'Step' axis is the evaluated stream, not a round count, and sits next to figures whose x-axis IS a round count.
unfavorable_facts.source: [Fig. 2 p.5; Fig. 5 p.7; Fig. 8a p.9; App. D.5 p.41; App. G.1 p.50; App. H.1.2 p.58; App. J.1.3 p.65]

unfavorable_facts.fact: Five incommensurable metrics are pooled under one thesis.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: AppWorld TGC%, ALFWorld task-success%, WebShop mean reward ×100 (and separately wins/50 and 'average score'), ARC-AGI %, ScienceWorld 'average test score' on an undefined scale. 'Memory utility degrades as consolidation continues' [Fig. 1 caption] ranges over all of them.
unfavorable_facts.source: [Fig. 1 p.2; Table 2 p.6; Table 3 p.15; App. F.3 p.47; App. J.1.3 p.65]

unfavorable_facts.fact: No no-memory reference line on several degradation figures.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: Fig. 16 prints two (15/48 and 19/48) and Fig. 2 prints the 100% ceiling, but Fig. 4 shows Start/From/To-Worst bars with Max-Drop annotations and no baseline, and Fig. 8b/8c show deltas only. The paper's central claim is 'can fall below the no-memory baseline', so a baseline line is the load-bearing element of every such figure.
unfavorable_facts.source: [Fig. 4 p.6; Fig. 8 p.9 vs Fig. 16 p.51, Fig. 2 p.5]

unfavorable_facts.fact: The paper is a diagnosis and says so — it proposes no gate, no architecture, and no repair.
unfavorable_facts.exact_wording: 'Our findings are diagnostic' [§9, p.12]; 'our diagnosis of failure modes does not constitute a fix' [§9, p.12]. Its two prescriptions (retain episodes; gate consolidation) are, by its own §1, in tension: 'episodic accumulation cannot be the long-term answer'.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: Not a flaw, but it bounds what the book may claim from it. The paper establishes that the current $\mathrm{wr}$ is a net loss under streaming; it does not establish that any $\mathrm{wr}$ must be.

unfavorable_facts.fact: The vendored text extraction of Table 2 is column-interleaved and the cell values used in this note are an editor reconstruction.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: The reconstruction is self-consistent under both caption rules with zero exceptions, which is strong evidence it is correct, but it is not the same as reading the PDF. No Table 2 cell should be printed in the book before the PDF check.

cross_path_citations.verdict: A NEW PATTERN for this corpus, and it is the mirror image of Letta STC's. The biological/CLS ancestry is cited HEAVILY and used as a load-bearing argument; the $W$-path and $\Theta$-path are cited ZERO times; the word 'sleep' appears ZERO times. Letta STC took the name and left the argument; this paper takes the argument and leaves the name.
cross_path_citations.term_counts_whole_text: 'sleep' (case-insensitive): 0. 'test-time': 0 outside the Dynamic Cheatsheet reference title. 'parametric': 1 (the §8 scope exclusion). 'consolidat*': 124.

bio_CLS_path.citations: HEAVY AND LOAD-BEARING. McClelland, McNaughton & O'Reilly 1995 (cited in §1, §2, §3, §5 — four separate sections); Squire et al. 2015; Dudai, Karni & Born 2015; Moscovitch et al. 2016; Kumaran, Hassabis & McClelland 2016; Tse et al. 2007 (Science, schemas and memory consolidation); Sun et al. 2023 (Nature Neuroscience, organizing memories for generalization in CLS); Bartlett 1932; Brainerd & Reyna 2002 (fuzzy-trace); Hintzman 1986; Brooks 1978; Medin & Schaffer 1978; Logan 1988 (the four instance-theory citations that justify the episodic-only control); McCloskey & Cohen 1989; French 1999; Zacks et al. 2007 (event segmentation); Flavell 1979, Nelson & Narens 1990, Koriat 1997 (metacognition).
bio_CLS_path.finding: This is not decoration. The CLS citation set (i) motivates the two-store architecture, (ii) is stated as a testable prediction, (iii) generates the three control loops, and (iv) supplies the interference mechanism the paper attributes its failures to. The instance-theory set (Hintzman, Brooks, Medin & Schaffer, Logan) is what licenses the episodic-only control as a theoretically motivated arm rather than an ad-hoc baseline: 'Schema-like behavior can emerge from in-context learning on preserved instances comparative to a separately stored abstraction' [§4.2, p.7]. The metacognition set supplies the paper's framing of the LLM as an unreliable monitor of its own abstractions.
bio_CLS_path.the_twist: It never says 'sleep'. Not once. The consolidation literature it cites is the same literature Letta STC borrowed the word from without citing.

E_path_internal.citations: Dense. MemGPT (Packer et al. 2023), Letta software doc (2024), Reflexion (Shinn et al. 2023), Generative Agents (Park et al. 2023), ExpeL (Zhao et al. 2024), Voyager (Wang et al. 2023), CLIN (Majumder et al. 2023), Mem0 (Chhikara et al. 2025), A-Mem (Xu et al. 2025), LangMem (LangChain AI 2024), ACE (Zhang et al. 2025), Dynamic Cheatsheet (Suzgun et al. 2026), ReasoningBank (Ouyang et al. 2026), CoALA (Sumers et al. 2024), PEARL (Li et al. 2026).
E_path_internal.the_absence_that_matters: Letta's `Sleep-time Compute` (2504.13171) is NOT cited. The paper cites the company's software page and the same team's MemGPT, but not the paper that named this line. So the founding-name paper of the $E$-path is invisible to the paper that measures the $E$-path's write operator over 200 rounds — and the reverse silence already holds (Letta STC cites nothing in agentic memory except MemGPT). [본서 관찰] ch15 already records that Mem0 and ReasoningBank do not cite Letta STC; this paper extends the pattern to the line's most direct critic.

W_path.citations: ZERO. No fast weights, no test-time training, no TTT/Titans/Miras/Atlas, no linear attention, no state-space models, no KV cache, no recurrent memory. The word 'cache' appears only in 'Dynamic Cheatsheet'.

Theta_path.citations: ZERO, with an explicit scope exclusion in place of a citation: 'parametric memory (weight updates, distillation into the model) and structured non-textual memory representations are out of scope' [§8, p.11]. No LoRA, no PEFT, no ROME/MEMIT, no SEAL, no continual learning, no EWC, no catastrophic-forgetting literature from the ML side — though McCloskey & Cohen 1989 and French 1999, the cognitive-science originals of catastrophic interference, ARE cited.
Theta_path.note: [note-writer] That last detail is the sharpest version of the corpus's silence pattern: the paper cites the 1989 and 1999 papers that named catastrophic interference and none of the thirty years of machine-learning work that tried to fix it.

cross_path_citations.adjacent: Turpin et al. 2023 (unfaithful chain-of-thought) is cited to support the claim that LLMs may not monitor their own abstractions — the paper's one bridge to the interpretability literature.
cross_path_citations.monograph_implication: [note-writer] For ch23/ch24 this paper is a genuine complication and should be written as one, not smoothed. The book's finding was that the sleep-time line borrowed a biological name without the biological argument. Here an $E$-path paper imports the biological argument in full — prediction, architecture, controls — and does not use the name at all. The correct chapter sentence is not '이 논문이 ch23을 반증한다' but '이름과 논증이 서로 다른 논문에 갈라져 실렸다': Letta STC has the word, this paper has the theory, and neither cites the other.

systems_implications.preamble: Grounding key: [PAPER] = a number or statement on the page with a locator; [INFERENCE] = the note-writer's translation. This paper contains no serving numbers at all, so almost everything here is [INFERENCE] from structure — but the structural facts it establishes are unusually consequential for serving.

items.claim: The $E$-path's offline write is not free even when it is off the critical path — it can be NEGATIVELY valued. A serving fleet running consolidation on idle capacity can spend $B_s$ to lower quality below the no-memory arm.
items.grounding: [PAPER] 16 of 28 consolidator cells in Table 2 sit below their row's no-memory baseline [본서 산술]; on AppWorld/GPT-5-Mini every one of ten memory conditions loses to NoMem = 23. [INFERENCE] The operational reading: the E-path's cost model is not 'pay $B_s$ once, save prefill many times' but 'pay $B_s$ once, and possibly pay again in quality'. Identity (A) has no term for a negative quality contribution.

items.claim: The single most actionable finding for a serving stack: KEEP THE POOL AND RE-DERIVE, do not rewrite the rewrite. At matched data and matched refresh count, whole-pool re-consolidation is stable and incremental consolidation collapses.
items.grounding: [PAPER] Static R10 = Static R50 = 94.7% against Stream R10 = 52.6% on the same 19 problems with the same ground-truth solutions [Fig. 2, p.5]. [본서 산술] 42.1 pp attributable to the schedule alone; $\rho_{\text{Static}} \approx 0.0$ pp per refresh over refreshes 2–50 versus $\rho_{\text{Stream}} = 0.249$ pp per update. [INFERENCE] In storage terms: a cold archive of raw episodes plus periodic full re-derivation dominates a hot mutable store that is edited in place. That is a concrete tier design, and it is the opposite of what every production $E$-path system in this corpus does.

items.claim: State bytes ARE computable from this paper, and they land where ch26's accounting put them.
items.grounding: [PAPER] 50 items / 48,506 characters at the cap; ~970 chars/item; ACE 32 bullets / ~14k chars; DC ~8.3k chars; AWM 16 workflows / ~8.2k chars [App. G.2 p.53; App. H.1.1 pp.56–57; App. H.1.2 p.58]. [본서 산술] 48,506 chars ≈ 48.5 KB at one byte per character, against ch26's 56.0 KB $E$-path anchor — agreement within 13.4%. [INFERENCE] The store is a cold-tier object read once per query, exactly as ch26 판정 2 classifies it. Nothing here moves the $E$-path out of the cold tier.

items.claim: The wake-side cost of a faulty entry is measurable in STEPS, and one bad entry moved it 8%.
items.grounding: [PAPER] Removing W8: mean steps 12.4 → 11.4 (gpt-5.4-mini) and 18.2 → 15.8 (gpt-5-mini); step-cap hits 22/50 → 17/50; page-turn actions 421 → 181 and 559 → 246 [Tables 12–13, p.61]. [INFERENCE] For an agent serving stack, a faulty memory entry is a token-consumption regression as well as a quality regression, and it shows up in the action histogram before it shows up in the reward. Action-category telemetry is therefore a cheaper faulty-memory detector than reward — a monitoring recommendation the paper does not make.

items.claim: Memory surgery is a per-entry attribution primitive that costs one re-evaluation and no training.
items.grounding: [PAPER] App. I: remove one item, hold policy and all other items fixed, re-evaluate. Result: 7/50 → 14/50 wins. [INFERENCE] This is a shipping-grade diagnostic: for a store of $n$ entries, $n$ re-evaluations price every entry. It generalises to any $E$-path system in the corpus and none of them do it. The book should carry it as a recommended falsifier form.

items.claim: shared-weight batching is untouched, as for every $E$-path system.
items.grounding: [INFERENCE] Nothing lands in weights; the store is application-level text spliced into the prompt. The $E$-path's structural serving advantage (ch27 A5) survives this paper entirely — and this paper, like the five before it, never mentions it.

items.claim: The offline write is a SEQUENTIAL chain of model turns whose length is the round count, and the round counts here are large.
items.grounding: [PAPER] 200 consolidation stages each rewriting the whole memory [App. G.1, p.50]; 190 update steps [App. D.5, p.41]; 3 abstraction calls per trajectory before any of it [App. F.1, p.45]. [INFERENCE] For the ALFWorld run that is 2304 abstraction calls + 200 full-memory rewrites per store [본서 산술]. At no point is that priced. A fleet operator reading this paper learns that the spending may be worth less than zero and cannot learn how much the spending is.

items.claim: Capacity pressure and quality are coupled through the write operator, not through the read path.
items.grounding: [PAPER] 'Memory size stays bounded at 38–50 items by the cap throughout, so the erosion is in content quality, not item count' [App. G.1, p.50]; and the paraphrase-cluster mode: '21 of the 38 items at stage 200 contain this opener. The desklamp directive only applies to look-at-in-light tasks, which are 8/48 of the eval split; the memory devotes 21/38 (>55%) of its prompt-context slots to it' [App. G.1, p.52]. [INFERENCE] Under a fixed prompt budget the relevant resource is not bytes but SLOT ALLOCATION, and the write operator reallocates slots away from rare-but-decisive entries toward frequent-but-generic ones. That is a compression-policy failure with an information-theoretic shape, and it is the closest thing in this corpus to a live instance of the rate–distortion problem ch22 discusses in the abstract.

items.claim: Byte-identical duplicates survive in a capped store because no pipeline dedups.
items.grounding: [PAPER] 'Items 3 and 5 of stage 200 are character-for-character identical, occupying two of the 50 cap slots with the same content. The pipeline applies no post-hoc deduplication step' [App. G.1, p.52]. Also visible at ScienceWorld round 1, where memories #1/#9 and #2/#10 are identical [App. J.1.3, p.65]. [INFERENCE] A one-line dedup pass would reclaim cap slots for free. That no system in this corpus has one is a shipping-quality observation, not a research one.

items.claim: The threshold-metric monitor fails exactly as ch29 predicted, but the failure shape is a third shape.
items.grounding: [PAPER] Fig. 16 shows a rise to a peak then a general decline 'with small recoveries' over 180 stages — gradual, not flat-then-cliff. Table 11 shows a single stage costing 12.5–27.1 pp — a cliff. [INFERENCE] The observed $E$-path shape is 'rise → gradual erosion punctuated by single-round cliffs', which is neither the smooth continuous decay nor the flat-then-cliff threshold curve X4 produced. A monitor set on the task metric would catch the cliff and miss the erosion; a monitor set on a rate would be calibrated 54–137× too low for the cliff [본서 산술].

discriminant_verdict.summary: PASSES all four conditions in its offline settings, on the $E$-path. Condition (1) is the only one requiring an argument, and it is also the condition the paper's own design straddles — so (1) is what decides the verdict.

conditions.verdict: PASS in the headline settings; FAIL in one named regime.
conditions.pass_evidence: In every setting that produces a table or an erosion curve, the store is built from a training pool and then read on a DISJOINT held-out split: ALFWorld `eval_id_balanced_48` [App. F.1, p.46]; WebShop `test50_seed42_no_leak.json` with the 13 overlapping training IDs excluded [App. F.2, p.47]; AppWorld's 100-task test subset drawn from the official test splits, disjoint from the 140 training trajectories [App. F.4, p.49]; ScienceWorld's 44-case test set evaluated 'after each full pass over all rollouts' [App. F.3, p.47]; ARC-AGI Stream 'Stream: offline GT-solution; eval on 50 held-out tasks (same family, unseen)' [Table 1, p.3].
conditions.fail_evidence: The 'Running' trajectory regime — 'where the agent learns from its own attempts as it solves new problems' [§3, p.5] — updates memory inside the stream it is scored on. Fig. 5's 400-step cumulative-success curve and ScienceWorld's 'self-solve task-switch sequence' [Table 1, p.3] are that regime. There the write is not before the query; it is between queries, exactly the MemGPT situation the book treats as a boundary case (→ ch13, ch11 §11.5).
conditions.why_this_is_the_deciding_condition: Because the paper is the first in the corpus to run BOTH sides of it under one design, and because the book's classification of this paper depends on which regime the chapter reads. The honest handling is the one ch11 §11.5 already established for MemGPT: admit it on the offline settings and name the regime that does not qualify.

conditions.verdict: PASS structurally; the budget is never reported in the book's units.
conditions.evidence: The write is an LLM call — 3 abstraction calls per trajectory [App. F.1, p.45] plus one full-memory rewrite per consolidation stage [App. G.1, p.50]. $B_s > 0$ is not in doubt. But no tokens, FLOPs, or dollars appear anywhere, so the cell stays 'absent' under ch25's rule. Note ch30 §30.3.3's observation that folding reporting quality into condition (2) would collapse the passing set — this paper would fall out under that variant too.

conditions.id: (3) $\Theta \cdot W \cdot E$ 중 한 층의 상태를 실제로 바꾼다
conditions.evidence: Textual memory banks are created, rewritten, capped, evicted, and deleted across up to 200 rounds. $\Theta$ is excluded by declaration: 'parametric memory (weight updates, distillation into the model) ... are out of scope' [§8, p.11]. $W$ is never mentioned.

'At evaluation we provide all memory entries in context' [§3, p.4]; 'The full memory is supplied in the prompt context at every step, so the rollout sees every item in every snapshot' [App. G.1, p.50]. $\mathrm{ret}$ is the identity, so the store's use is total and unconfounded by retrieval.

discriminant_verdict.which_condition_decides: **Condition (1).** (2)(3)(4) are satisfied trivially. (1) is satisfied by the offline settings and violated by the Running regime, so the verdict is a PASS conditioned on which settings the chapter cites — and the chapter must name the split rather than let the paper enter as a monolith. Secondarily, condition (2) decides how much the paper can be used FOR: it passes the discriminant while leaving $B_s$ unreported, so it can settle $\rho$ questions and cannot settle amortisation questions.
discriminant_verdict.path_assignment: $E$-path. Not a system proposal but an instrumentation of $\mathrm{wr}$; it belongs beside Mem0/Zep/ReasoningBank/SCM in ch15's group, or as the closing section of that chapter.
discriminant_verdict.count_consequence: If admitted, the book's counting convention '통과 9 + 경계 1 + 불충족 19 = 29' (PRE-RESEARCH §2.2) becomes '통과 10 + 경계 1 + 불충족 19 = 30', and the path split $E$ 6 / $W$ 1 / $\Theta$ 2 becomes $E$ 7 / $W$ 1 / $\Theta$ 2. Every aggregate in ch11 §11.3.1, ch24, ch27 표 27-1 A1 and 부록 C moves. The alternative is to hold the corpus at its 2026-08 boundary and cite this paper as post-corpus evidence in Part III only. **That is an editorial decision, not a factual one, and the chapter must state which it took.**

book_impact.summary: This paper touches eight chapters. It BREAKS one pre-registered corpus census (ch29 판정 6's '$K>100$ 실험 0편'), THREATENS three (ch25 표 25-1's $\rho$ row, ch27 §27.2 C2, ch26 판정 6 / 요약), CONFIRMS four (ch27 판정 2, ch29 판정 4, ch29 판정 5, ch26 판정 2), COMPLICATES one (ch23 §23.8 / ch30 표 30-3의 생물학 행), and adds a new caveat to one (ch14's reading of Letta STC's headline numbers).

breaks.the_book_s_sentence: "셋째, **$K^\ast$** — 반복 지평이 기회의 크기를 정하는데 100회를 넘긴 실험이 0편이고, 라운드당 열화율을 라운드 수의 함수로 인쇄한 논문도 0편이다."
breaks.what_breaks_it: This paper runs 200 consolidation stages (ALFWorld), 190 update steps and 250 single-pass steps (ARC-AGI), 192 stages (ACE on WebShop), 100 distill iterations (Fig. 8a), and 400 stream steps — and prints quality as a function of the round index with no-memory reference lines. Both clauses of the sentence are false as written.

confirms.target: ch27 판정 2 — and this is the strongest new evidence the book could have received for it.
confirms.the_book_s_verdict: "$E$-경로는 유망하다. 단 **비용 방법으로서**다. 품질 방법으로서는 현재 문헌이 지지하지 않으며, 그 반증은 이 책이 아니라 논문들 자신의 표에서 나온다."
confirms.what_confirms_it: [본서 산술] 26 of 28 consolidator cells in Table 2 are beaten by a raw-trajectory-log baseline; 16 of 28 fall below no-memory; on AppWorld 31 of 40 memory cells of every kind fall below no-memory and for GPT-5-Mini every single one does; on WebShop ACE = 0.00 and DC = 0.03 against NoMem = 0.18; and 'Abstract Only stays at or below the zero-shot baseline throughout' [Fig. 17, p.69]. Plain in-context learning on the family reaches 86% against every memory configuration below it [Fig. 9b, p.10]. This is a fifth, sixth and seventh independent system showing the pattern ch15 §15.6 found in Mem0, Zep, SCM and ReasoningBank.
confirms.what_it_ADDS_to_the_verdict: ch27 판정 2's cost half assumes quality parity: '프롬프트를 26k에서 수백 토큰으로 줄이면 prefill이 준다 — 이득의 방향은 구조적으로 참이다'. That argument is valid only against a no-memory arm of comparable quality. **This paper shows the quality can go BELOW no-memory, at which point the cost comparison is not 'same quality, cheaper' but 'worse than free, and you paid $B_s$ for it'.** The chapter should add a clause: 비용 이득의 방향은 여전히 구조적으로 참이지만, 그 논증은 품질이 no-memory 팔 아래로 내려가지 않는 레짐에서만 의미가 있고, 반복 (U-E) 하에서 그 전제가 실증적으로 깨진다.

confirms.the_book_s_verdict: "반복이 이 기회의 시간 지평을 정하고, 반복은 보존된 원본 아카이브를 요구한다. 그러므로 $\Theta$-경로는 $E$-경로를 대체하지 않는다." — supported by X4 F6 (원본 앵커 replay가 자기 출력 앵커보다 모든 $\omega$에서 오래 버틴다) and [Continual Facts §6.2]'s frozen-teacher contrast.
confirms.what_confirms_it: The Static-vs-Stream control is the same sign in a third, independent place, on a different layer, with a real LLM: re-deriving from the PRESERVED POOL at every refresh holds 94.7% across 50 refreshes; rewriting the previous rewrite falls to 52.6% on identical data [Fig. 2, p.5]. And the paper's own diagnosis is the anchoring mechanism: 'early abstractions can anchor later rewrites and mistakes are reused as context for future consolidation, so small errors in segmentation or abstraction compound' [§4.1, p.6].
confirms.why_this_matters_for_the_grade: ch29 판정 4 carries the caveat 'X4는 LLM 실험이 아니므로 이 판정이 X4에서 받는 것은 **부호와 순서뿐**'. The sign now has a real-LLM instance. The judgment's evidence grade rises from (minimal model + one $\Theta$-path paper's contrast) to (minimal model + $\Theta$-path contrast + a 200-round $E$-path experiment). **And it generalises the claim: the preserved-original archive is not a $\Theta$-path requirement, it is a requirement of iterated rewriting as such.**
confirms.strength: CONFIRM, with a grade upgrade and a scope widening.

confirms.the_book_s_verdict: "운영 지표는 라운드당 열화율이 아니라 crossover $K^\ast$여야 하고, 감시는 임계 과제 지표가 아니라 연속 신호에 걸어야 한다." — with the supporting sentence "그리고 라운드당 비율은 라운드에 대해 상수가 아니므로 SLA로 걸 수 있는 양이 아니다."
confirms.what_confirms_it: [본서 산술] The ALFWorld mean rate is 0.198–0.231 pp per consolidation stage; a single stage (S=168→169) costs 12.5–27.1 pp. That is 54× to 137× the mean, in the same run, on the same benchmark. $\rho$ is empirically not constant in $k$ — the book asserted this from a minimal model and now has it from an LLM loop. And $K^\ast$ is directly readable and behaves as the book said an operational quantity should: $K^\ast = 20$ stages (Qwen3.5-4B, 9B), $K^\ast = 0$ (Qwen3.5-27B).

So the $E$-path shape is a third shape — erosion punctuated by cliffs. The chapter should print that as an observation rather than force it into X4's two-curve story.
confirms.strength: CONFIRM the first half and the non-constancy; leave the second half open; report the shape tension.
